section_title: How did the Lord sustain Paul when no one stood with him?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 16 At my first defense, no one stood with me, but everyone deserted me. May it not be charged against them. 17 But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the message would be fully proclaimed, and all the Gentiles would hear it. So I was delivered from the mouth of the lion. 18 And the Lord will rescue me from every evil action and bring me safely into His heavenly kingdom. To Him be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

context_lines: Paul recalls standing without human support at his first defense. He asks that the abandonment not be charged against those who failed him. He then names the support that remained: the Lord stood by him and gave him strength.
That strength served a purpose beyond his own survival. The message was proclaimed so that the Gentiles could hear. Paul describes his rescue as deliverance from a lion’s mouth.
He trusts the Lord to bring him safely into His heavenly kingdom. Since he has just spoken of approaching death, this confidence is larger than a promise to avoid physical harm indefinitely.
common_interpretation_lines: [Calvin](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/2_timothy/4.htm) understands the lion’s mouth as a picture of severe danger rather than necessarily a literal lion or one specific ruler. He reads the final rescue especially as God keeping Paul faithful and bringing him into the kingdom. [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-second-epistle-to-timothy/) likewise distinguishes that final safety from merely escaping death.
The shared encouragement is that human abandonment does not leave Paul outside God’s care. His trust rests in the Lord who strengthens and keeps him, even when faithful service remains costly.
god_plan_lines: [Daniel 6:19–27](https://biblehub.com/bsb/daniel/6.htm) offers a related picture: God rescues His servant from lions, and that rescue leads to a proclamation of His enduring kingdom among the nations. This is a biblical parallel, not a claim that Paul is reporting a literal lions’ den.

Paul directly connects his own rescue with the Gentiles hearing the message. [Acts 23:11](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/23.htm) similarly records the Lord standing near Paul and assuring him of witness in Rome. God’s keeping serves His mission, while the letter’s final hope reaches into His heavenly kingdom.
